title: Counter loop escape witness
statement: Let $M$ be a deterministic machine with $k$ work tapes and distinct states $a$ and $ex$, and let $e:\\{0,1\\}\\hookrightarrow\\Gamma$ encode Boolean symbols. Let $w$ be a Boolean word and suppose the extra tape initially agrees with its encoded word buffer at cells $cp+p$ for every integer $p$ with $-1\\le p\\le |w|$. For an initial configuration $c$, run-length function $\\tau$, and property $P$ of the first $k$ work-head positions, choose $r_0$ strictly below the binary value of $w$. Suppose every round $r\\le r_0$ satisfies the round conditions for exit set $\\{some\\ ex\\}$ and property $P$, and the configuration after round $r_0$ is in state $ex$. Then after $\\sum_{r\\le r_0}\\tau(c_r)+\\operatorname{overhead}(w,r_0+1)$ steps, the counter-loop machine is in its escape configuration, with the extra tape on the word cells holding the encoded buffer of the counter word after $r_0+1$ decrements. Before the endpoint its state is never halting, done, or escape; through the endpoint the extra head remains in $[cp-1,cp+|w|]$, and at each time the first $k$ head positions match those of some run of $M$ from a round configuration, with either $r\\le r_0$ and $u\\le\\tau(c_r)$ or $r=r_0+1$ and $u=0$.

Every round $r\\le r_0$ satisfies the round conditions
The configuration after round $r_0$ has state $ex$
